 Shri C.K. Misrha- G.A. for the State.
Shri Pradeep Singh Chouhan- advocate for the objector

Order
This first application under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita has been filed on behalf of the applicants for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.260/2025 of Police Station- Kotwali District Betul (MP) for commission of the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC for grant of anticipatory bail.
3.Prosecution story, in brief, is that applicant repeatedly established physical relation with prosecutrix, aged 32-33 years on the false pretext of marriage.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant as well as prosecutrix were in relationship since 2023 and FIR has been lodged on 4.3.2025.
Marriage of the parties was also fixed.
It is a case of consensual relationship.
Applicant has been falsely implicated.
Therefore, learned counsel for the applicant prays for grant of anticipatory bail.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17212 2 MCRC-15083-2025 Chitranjan Ivane vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19289900/
1
5 . Per-contra, learned counsel for the objector as well as State submit that initially marriage of the applicant was fixed with the prosecutrix, but later on applicant refused to marry prosecutrix.
Applicant has deceived prosecutrix and established physical relation with her on the false pretext of marriage.
Hence, application filed applicant be dismissed.

6. Having regard to the facts as mentioned in the FIR as well as in the statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

7. It is directed that in the event of his arrest, present applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

It is also directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions as enumerated under Section 482 (2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023.

8.It is made clear that applicant shall appear before the Investigating Officer as & when he is so directed and co-operate with the investigation and he shall also appear before the Trial Court failing which his bail shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
9. Certified copy as per rules.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Ansari Chitranjan Ivane vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19289900/
